brief: A three-storey red-brick hotel on a downtown corner: rows of white-framed windows under a bracketed cornice, a ground floor of restaurant and bar fronts behind a long porch roof and awnings, flags on the corner. Two photos. Older than 1970: Lake Erie island and harbour-town main streets (the Put-in-Bay model) are 19th-century commercial blocks; no newer example of this main-street type exists. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the Island House hotel (Port Clinton OH, 1886): a three-storey red brick Italianate hotel on a corner, arched windows with hoods and white shutters, iron balconettes, a bracketed cornice with the date panel, a later entry portico and a navy awning; decorative lamps
